title: Batch 7 Second Temple / Hellenistic Curation Methodology
notes: Separates ancient literary testimony, canonical Scripture references, securely dated geopolitical events, archaeological site identification, inscriptions/papyri, and modern scholarly reconstruction. Hellenistic and Hasmonean political polygons are broad orientation only, not surveyed borders.
verificationNote: Project-authored curation methodology; no external source verification claim is implied.

title: A History of the Jews and Judaism in the Second Temple Period — Hellenistic and Hasmonean volumes
author: Lester L. Grabbe
notes: Critical historical synthesis used for Hellenistic Judea, the Maccabean revolt, Hasmonean rule, and source criticism. Exact chronology and institutional interpretations are cross-checked rather than copied as map geometry.

title: The History of the Jewish People in the Age of Jesus Christ (175 B.C.–A.D. 135), revised edition
author: Emil Schürer; revised by Géza Vermes, Fergus Millar, Matthew Black and Martin Goodman
notes: Major reference for Seleucid, Hasmonean, Roman and Herodian chronology and institutions.

title: 1 Maccabees
organization: Ancient Jewish historical narrative preserved in the Septuagint/deuterocanonical tradition
dateLabel: Late second century BCE is commonly proposed for composition
notes: Primary ancient literary source for the revolt and early Hasmonean dynasty. It is not bundled as part of the project’s default BSB Protestant-canon text and is treated as an ancient source rather than as archaeological proof.

title: 2 Maccabees
organization: Ancient Jewish epitome of a work attributed to Jason of Cyrene
dateLabel: Hellenistic period; exact composition date debated
notes: Ancient literary source especially important for the Jerusalem crisis under Antiochus IV and temple-centered memory. Its literary/theological aims are kept distinct from independent archaeological evidence.

title: Josephus, Jewish Antiquities, Book 12
author: Flavius Josephus
notes: Later ancient narrative for Ptolemaic/Seleucid Judea and the Maccabean revolt. Josephus often depends on earlier sources and must not be treated as a contemporary inscription.

title: Josephus, Jewish Antiquities, Book 13
author: Flavius Josephus
notes: Major ancient narrative for Hasmonean rulers, expansion, internal conflict and neighboring peoples; used critically alongside archaeology and earlier evidence.

title: Josephus, Jewish Antiquities, Book 14
author: Flavius Josephus
notes: Ancient narrative for Pompey, Hyrcanus II, Aristobulus II, Antipater and the Roman transition.

title: Josephus, Jewish War, Book 1
author: Flavius Josephus
notes: Ancient narrative for late Hasmonean politics, Pompey, Herod’s rise and early Herodian rule; checked against Antiquities and Roman sources.

title: Arrian, Anabasis of Alexander
author: Arrian of Nicomedia
dateLabel: Second century CE, using earlier Alexander traditions
notes: Key later ancient narrative for Alexander’s campaigns. The atlas uses it for broad campaign sequence, not for claiming an exact march line.

title: Polybius, Histories
author: Polybius
notes: Near-contemporary ancient history for Hellenistic interstate politics, including Antiochus III and the Ptolemaic-Seleucid struggle. Surviving coverage is incomplete.

title: Diodorus Siculus, Library of History
author: Diodorus Siculus
notes: Ancient narrative useful for Alexander and successor-era context, employed critically where the surviving text bears on events.

title: Appian, Syrian Wars
author: Appian of Alexandria
notes: Later ancient source for Seleucid and Roman eastern history; used as contextual evidence, not as a cartographic authority.

title: Strabo, Geography
author: Strabo
dateLabel: Late first century BCE to early first century CE
notes: Ancient geographic description for the eastern Mediterranean and Near East. Place descriptions are cross-checked against archaeology.

title: Zenon Archive papyri
notes: Contemporary documentary evidence for Ptolemaic administration, travel and economic networks in Egypt and the southern Levant; not a political-border dataset.

title: Heliodorus / Seleucus IV administrative stele tradition
notes: Inscriptional evidence for Seleucid temple-administration policy in Coele-Syria/Phoenicia. It provides context for the period but is not treated as proof of every scene in 2 Maccabees 3.

title: Mount Gerizim Excavations and Samaritan temple precinct publications
author: Yitzhak Magen and excavation teams
notes: Archaeological basis for the Persian/Hellenistic sanctuary and settlement on Mount Gerizim. The destruction phase is correlated cautiously with Hasmonean historical testimony.

title: Maresha archaeological publications
author: Amos Kloner and collaborators
notes: Used for Hellenistic Maresha/Marisa, its Idumean and cosmopolitan material culture, subterranean complexes and destruction/transition history.

title: The Archaeology of Qumran and the Dead Sea Scrolls
author: Jodi Magness
notes: Archaeological synthesis for Khirbet Qumran, settlement phases and material culture. The identity of the community and its relation to the scroll caves remain interpretive questions.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls Today
author: James C. VanderKam
notes: General scholarly reference for manuscript corpus, dating, provenance questions and Second Temple Jewish diversity.

title: Herod: King of the Jews and Friend of the Romans
author: Peter Richardson
notes: Historical synthesis for Herod’s rise, Roman relations, administration and building program.

title: The Architecture of Herod, the Great Builder
author: Ehud Netzer
notes: Archaeological/architectural synthesis for Herodian palaces, fortresses, Caesarea, Herodium and Jerusalem. Reconstructed elevations are not treated as directly preserved in full.

title: Rome and the Arabian Frontier: From the Nabataeans to the Saracens
author: David F. Graf
notes: Historical and archaeological context for Nabataean territory, caravan networks and the Roman eastern frontier.

title: Cleopatra: A Biography
author: Duane W. Roller
notes: Historical synthesis for Cleopatra VII, Antony, Herod and eastern Mediterranean politics in the late first century BCE.

title: Plutarch, Lives of Pompey and Antony
author: Plutarch
dateLabel: Late first to early second century CE
notes: Later ancient biographical evidence for Roman eastern politics. Narrative details are cross-checked with Josephus and other Roman evidence.

title: Judaism and Hellenism
author: Martin Hengel
notes: Influential synthesis on Hellenistic cultural interaction in Judea and the eastern Mediterranean. Used as interpretive context, not as a source of exact map boundaries.

title: The Sacred Bridge: Carta’s Atlas of the Biblical World
author: Anson F. Rainey and R. Steven Notley
notes: Reference for historical geography and chronological orientation. No proprietary atlas geometry is copied; project coordinates and polygons are independently curated and uncertainty-labelled.
